requirements.requirement: On node1, run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as the managed service inventory-worker under the dedicated inventorysvc account.
requirements.summary: The executor created the dedicated inventorysvc system account, installed and enabled inventory-worker.service with the required executable and account, and directly observed the active process running with inventorysvc UID/GID 992. After node restart, the service was again enabled, active, and running under UID 992.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: Before execution and after the restart, node1 remained Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. The implementation used the platform-native systemd service manager, passed systemd unit verification, and the command timeline shows no software installation or OS/kernel replacement.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart service and boot ID were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the post-restart boot ID differed, and the system and service recovered. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart, and final lifecycle checks show a healthy node without unwanted exposure or residue.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed state-changing actions had clear roles: creating the required account, installing and enabling the required unit, and performing the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary mutation was identified. Temporary unit-file staging was cleaned by its trap, while post-restart temporary-directory differences are normal systemd PrivateTmp directories. The final node had no failed units, no new listening sockets, and healthy package-manager state.
